limitations: Source-derived candidate; no local efficacy validation.
Original typed source inventory is not normalized; retain source identities and limits in the procedure/readsets.

applicability.scope: Build, measure and diagnose one Ascend operator in isolation using msprof op, before interpreting system-level or multi-kernel performance.
applicability.prerequisites: A built executable or test harness and access to real NPU hardware with msprof op for collection.
applicability.input_contract: Operator executable/harness, collection settings and OPPROF output directory, plus the operator directory used to archive each measurement round.
applicability.produced_artifact: Per-round raw CSV archives and observational min/average/max summaries, followed by a bottleneck interpretation and comparison of operator duration and core balance.
applicability.failure_modes: Unwarmed or reduced-frequency runs distort timing; separately budgeting simultaneous GM reads/writes misses shared bandwidth, and tiny workloads can be dominated by launch overhead.

recommendations: Collect warmup and repeated measurements into a named round, preserve the raw CSVs, and distinguish the summary statistics from the subsequent bottleneck judgment.
Compare task duration, dominant pipeline ratios and per-core balance together; change one optimization point, rebuild as needed and archive the new round before deciding to keep it.
Check current versus rated frequency and shared read/write bandwidth before blaming the kernel; aggregate msprof ratios do not provide an instruction-by-instruction timeline.
